facts: The compound mixed team event was added to the 2028 program in April 2025, making it the first compound medal event at the Games and the first new bowstyle since archery returned to the Games in 1972.

The host nation gets three recurve quota places per gender and one compound mixed team place, provided it enters the corresponding teams at the 2027 World Archery Championships.

facts: The men's and women's half-marathon race walk finals are both scheduled in a single morning session from 7:30 to 11:35 a.m. on Thursday, July 27, 2028.
The order of the two races within the July 27 session had not been announced when the athletics schedule was released in November 2025.
Track and field events at the 2028 Games run at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum from July 15-24, so the race walks take place after the track program ends.
The women's marathon is scheduled for July 29 and the men's marathon for July 30, the final day of the 2028 Games, with the marathons using a Venice Beach Boardwalk start.
The race walk venue and course for the 2028 Games had not been announced as of November 2026.

The 2028 Games replace the 20 km walks with half-marathon (21.1 km) race walks for men and women; the half marathon and marathon race walks became official World Athletics distances on January 1, 2026.
World Athletics published the 2028 Games athletics qualification system in November 2026, setting the race walk qualification window from December 19, 2026 to June 18, 2028.

The top 12 finishers at the World Athletics Race Walking Team Championships in Hefei, China, on April 9, 2028 automatically qualify for the half-marathon race walks at the 2028 Games, with the remaining 36 places in each event allocated through world rankings.

Spain's Maria Perez, the Paris 2024 20 km silver medalist, set the inaugural women's half-marathon race walk world record of 1:30:06 while winning the European title in Birmingham on August 15, 2026, on her debut at the distance.
Perez also holds the world record for the 35 km race walk.
Spain's Paul McGrath won the men's half-marathon race walk at the 2026 European Championships in Birmingham in 1:23:23, giving Spain a sweep of both half-marathon walk titles.

The mixed marathon race walk relay, held only at Paris 2024, has been dropped from the 2028 program to make room for a mixed 4x100m relay, and Canada's Evan Dunfee publicly criticized the move as part of the 'ongoing TikTokification' of the Games.
At Paris 2024, Ecuador's Brian Pintado won the men's 20 km walk, Brazil's Caio Bonfim took silver and Spain's Alvaro Martin took bronze.
At Paris 2024, China's Yang Jiayu won the women's 20 km walk, Spain's Maria Perez took silver and Australia's Jemima Montag took bronze.
Spain won the Paris 2024 mixed marathon race walk relay ahead of Ecuador and Australia, so those three nations each won medals in two of the three race walk events at Paris 2024.

Venezuela won the 2026 World Baseball Classic, defeating the United States 3-2 in the final on March 17, 2026, in front of a sold-out crowd of 36,190 at loanDepot Park in Miami.
It was Venezuela's first World Baseball Classic title; Wilyer Abreu and Eugenio Suarez delivered key hits in the final, and Maikel Garcia was named tournament MVP.

Bryce Harper hit a two-run home run in the eighth inning of the 2026 Classic final to tie the score before Venezuela won, and the loss was the second straight Classic final defeat for the United States after losing to Japan in 2023.
Venezuela will make its first appearance in baseball at the Games in 2028 after qualifying through the 2026 World Baseball Classic.
The United States qualified automatically as host and reached the 2026 Classic final by beating the Dominican Republic 2-1 in the semifinal, with Paul Skenes starting.

Three further places will come from the 2027 WBSC Premier12 and a final qualifier held no later than March 2028, so 2020 champion Japan and 2024 Premier12 champion Chinese Taipei have not yet qualified.

MLB owners reportedly support an 11-day season pause tied to the 2028 All-Star break so active major leaguers could play, but no agreement with the players' union had been announced as of November 2026.
MLB's collective bargaining agreement expires December 1, 2026, and owners were expected to begin a lockout the next day, per Sportico.
Meyer said in March 2026 that losing the 2027 MLB season to a work stoppage would knock big leaguers out of the 2028 Games.
A United States-Venezuela gold medal game would be a rematch of the 2026 World Baseball Classic final, though the finalists depend on the semifinal results.

facts: The organizing committee announced on May 8, 2025 that the 2028 Opening Ceremony will be held across two stadiums at the same time, the LA Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park and SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, which no previous edition of the modern Games has done.
The official schedule lists the Opening Ceremony on Day 0, Friday, July 14, 2028, at 5:00 p.m. PT (8:00 p.m. ET).

SoFi Stadium will be called the 2028 Stadium (also referred to as the Stadium in Inglewood) during the Games; it opened in September 2020 and is home to the NFL's Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers.
SoFi Stadium will also host swimming during the 2028 Games, and the Games will be its first.
The LA Memorial Coliseum opened in 1923 and hosted the Opening Ceremonies of the 1932 and 1984 Summer Games, which makes 2028 its third Games.
In a Los Angeles City Council vote in November 2025 that moved the Closing Ceremony entirely to the Coliseum, the two-stadium plan for the Opening Ceremony was kept unchanged.

On October 28, 2026, organizers named film producer Kathleen Kennedy, former president of Lucasfilm, as Head of Ceremonies and Content; she will serve as an Executive Producer of the Opening and Closing Ceremonies.
Kennedy took over the role from Peter Rice, who stays on as an Executive Producer of the ceremonies after being named Netflix's Chief Content Officer in October 2026.
The ceremonies team also includes Ben Winston as Executive Producer and Creative Director, and longtime Games ceremonies producer Scott Givens as Executive Producer of Production.
Kennedy said that she and her husband, producer Frank Marshall, have attended almost every Games since Los Angeles 1984.
Official hospitality packages list the Opening Ceremony as session CER01A at 17:00 PT on Friday, July 14, 2028.
Reports from the 2025-2026 ticket sales said top Opening Ceremony seats went for more than $5,000 each, and ticket prices drew public complaints about cost.
According to the schedule, the first medals of the 2028 Games will be awarded in the women's triathlon after the Opening Ceremony.

facts: The official schedule lists the Closing Ceremony on Day 16, Sunday, July 30, 2028, at 6:00 p.m. PT (9:00 p.m. ET).

The Closing Ceremony was first planned to be split between the LA Memorial Coliseum and SoFi Stadium, but in November 2025 the Los Angeles City Council voted unanimously to hold it entirely at the Coliseum in Exposition Park.
Los Angeles Councilmember Marqueece Harris-Dawson said the change was meant to confirm the Coliseum as one of the only buildings in the world to host three Games opening or closing ceremonies.
The LA Memorial Coliseum opened in 1923, was built to attract the Games, and hosted the Opening Ceremonies of the 1932 and 1984 Summer Games.
The Coliseum will host both competition and ceremonies in 2028 and is expected to become the first venue to host events at three Summer Games.

On October 28, 2026, organizers named producer Kathleen Kennedy, former president of Lucasfilm, as Head of Ceremonies and Content, with responsibility for shaping the Games' farewell at the Closing Ceremony.

Peter Rice, Kennedy's predecessor and now Netflix's Chief Content Officer, stays on as an Executive Producer; Ben Winston is Executive Producer and Creative Director, and Scott Givens is Executive Producer of Production.
The Paralympic Closing Ceremony will also be held at the Coliseum, on August 27, 2028, after a Paralympic Opening Ceremony at the 2028 Stadium in Inglewood on August 15, 2028.

At the Paris 2024 Closing Ceremony, Los Angeles received the flag in a handover segment that included Tom Cruise and a pre-recorded Los Angeles program with Billie Eilish, Snoop Dogg and the Red Hot Chili Peppers.

facts: The 2028 Games road cycling time trials are scheduled for July 19, 2028, with men's and women's individual events.
Organizers confirmed on June 9, 2026 that the time trial courses will start at the Los Angeles Zoo in Griffith Park and finish at Griffith Observatory, both in the Griffith Park Zone.
The organizing committee describes the time trial as a challenging 35km course, with full course routes to be unveiled before the end of 2026.
The road races follow on July 22 (women, 150km) and July 23 (men, 250km), starting at Venice Beach Boardwalk and also finishing at Griffith Observatory.

The Griffith Observatory finish means the time trial course is expected to include a climb into the hills of Griffith Park, though exact gradients have not been published as of the June 2026 announcement.
The Los Angeles Zoo will also serve as the start and finish for para cycling road events on August 22-26, 2028.
Cycling Road at the 2028 Games will feature an equal number of men's and women's participants and events.
Remco Evenepoel of Belgium won the men's time trial at Paris 2024 ahead of Filippo Ganna of Italy and Wout Van Aert of Belgium.
Evenepoel won the men's individual time trial at the 2025 UCI Road World Championships in Kigali, Rwanda, finishing ahead of Tadej Pogacar for his third straight world time trial title.
Grace Brown of Australia won the women's time trial at Paris 2024 in 39:38.24, ahead of Anna Henderson of Great Britain and Chloe Dygert of the USA.
Brown retired at the end of the 2024 season, so the women's event at the 2028 Games will crown a new champion.
Neither Evenepoel nor Ganna has been confirmed as a 2028 Games time trial entrant as of the latest available reports.

facts: The 2028 Games women's road race is scheduled for July 22, 2028, starting at the Venice Beach Boardwalk and finishing at Griffith Observatory in Griffith Park.
Organizers announced in June 2026 that both road races will finish at Griffith Observatory; the route runs from the Pacific coastline through urban areas into the hills overlooking Los Angeles.
The 2028 women's road race course is listed by organizers at 150 km, compared with 250 km for the men.
The final climb to Griffith Observatory is reported at about 3.9 km with roughly 190 m of elevation gain, an average gradient of 4.9 percent and steepest sections around 6.7 percent.
The full turn-by-turn road race route had not been published as of the latest available reports.
The Venice Beach Boardwalk, LA Zoo and Griffith Observatory will all be used as competition venues at a Games for the first time in 2028.
The UCI qualification system for the 2028 Games allocates 90 road cycling quota places per gender across the road race and time trial.
At Paris 2024, Kristen Faulkner (USA) won gold, Marianne Vos (NED) took silver and Lotte Kopecky (BEL) took bronze in the women's road race.
Faulkner's Paris 2024 win was the first US medal of any color in the road race since the 1984 Los Angeles Games; she has not publicly confirmed 2028 participation per available sources.
Demi Vollering (NED) won the 2026 UCI Road World Championships women's road race in Montreal on September 26, 2026, her first world road title, outsprinting Poland's Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney.
Italy's Elisa Longo Borghini took bronze at the 2026 Worlds women's road race, which was 180.1 km from Brossard to Montreal.
Vollering attacked solo on Mont-Royal with a little under 40 km to go at the 2026 Worlds before being joined by Niewiadoma-Phinney and winning a two-rider sprint in 4:45:09.
Vollering's career wins include the Tour de France Femmes, Giro d'Italia Women, Vuelta Femenina and European Championships; a gold from the Games is one of the few major titles she lacks.
Vollering joined a Specialized social ride in the Los Angeles area in late October 2026 alongside Remco Evenepoel.
Canada's Magdeleine Vallieres Mill won the 2025 world road race title in Kigali, ahead of Niamh Fisher-Black (NZL) and Mavi Garcia (ESP).
The 2028 Tour de France has been moved to June 24 to July 16, 2028, to avoid a conflict with the Games.

The women's tournament at the 2028 Games has 16 teams, up from 12 at Paris 2024, and the United States qualified automatically as host.
Brazil, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, qualified for the 2028 women's tournament by beating Uruguay 5-1 in the 2025 Copa America Femenina semifinals.

The 2026 Concacaf W Championship, played November 27 to December 5, 2026 in Mansfield and Houston, Texas, sends its two finalists and third-place team to the 2028 Games, with the fourth-place team qualifying if the U.S. finishes in the top three.

The U.S. opens the Concacaf W Championship against El Salvador on November 27, 2026 in Mansfield, and Emma Hayes named a 51-player preliminary roster including Trinity Rodman, Lindsey Heaps, Naomi Girma and Lily Yohannes.

UEFA's four women's places will go to the four League A group winners of the 2027 UEFA Women's Nations League, which starts in February 2027; the draw put England with France, Austria and Portugal, and world champion Spain with Norway, Ireland and Switzerland.
Germany, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, was drawn into a 2027 Nations League League A group with the Netherlands, Sweden and Scotland.

Sixteen African teams, including Morocco, Nigeria, Ghana, Zambia, South Africa and Cameroon, advanced to the third round of Africa's women's qualifying, set for February 23 to March 6, 2027, with two places available.
Asia's women's qualifying tournament gives two direct places, and its third-place team meets Argentina in an AFC-CONMEBOL play-off.
Spain beat the U.S. on October 10, 2026 at Audi Field in Washington after the U.S. fell 2-0 behind and missed a second-half penalty.
The United States beat Brazil 1-0 in the Paris 2024 final on a Mallory Swanson goal to win a record fifth women's gold, and Germany won bronze.
The women's gold medal match is scheduled for July 29, 2028 at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena; team matchups will be set after qualification and a draw.

facts: Etihad Park in Willets Point, Queens, holds about 25,000, will be New York City FC's home and is set to open July 17, 2027 for the start of the 2027-28 MLS season.
NYCFC plans to soft-launch Etihad Park with a series of test events starting in April 2027.
Etihad Park will be called New York Stadium during the Games and will host nine matches, with group games on July 10-11, 13-14 and 16-17 and a men's quarterfinal on July 20, 2028.
The men's tournament at the 2028 Games has 12 teams, down from 16 at Paris 2024, and the United States qualified automatically as host, leaving 11 places for teams from six confederations.
The FIFA Council approved the final allocation of men's berths in December 2025; as of September 2026, CONMEBOL and OFC had not announced their qualifying formats.

Mexico, the London 2012 men's champion, qualified for the 2028 men's tournament in August 2026 by beating Canada 2-1 in the Concacaf U-20 Championship semifinals at Estadio Azteca after trailing at half-time.
Asia's two direct men's places will go to the top two finishers at the 2028 AFC U-23 Asian Cup in Japan, scheduled for January 4-22, 2028.
U.S. Soccer named Steve Cherundolo, a three-time World Cup player and former MLS Cup-winning LAFC coach, as head coach of the U.S. U-23 men's team for the 2028 Games on July 9, 2026.

Cherundolo named 23 players for the first U.S. U-23 camp of the cycle, held November 9-17, 2026 in San Pedro del Pinatar, Spain, with matches against Scotland on November 15 and Ukraine on November 17.

Spain won the Paris 2024 men's gold by beating host France 5-3 after extra time, with Fermin Lopez scoring twice and Sergio Camello scoring in extra time; Morocco won bronze, its first medal in the sport.
The men's gold medal match is scheduled for July 28, 2028 at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, and the full men's field and draw had not been set as of November 2026.

The U.S. women hold the host place; the women's tournament runs 13-28 July 2028.

The U.S. men beat Canada 12-11 in the 2026 Pan-American Sixes final in Oshawa, and Haudenosaunee beat Puerto Rico 15-13 for bronze.

Canada beat the United States in the men's Sixes gold medal game at The World Games 2022 in Birmingham, Alabama.
Andy Shay is head coach of the U.S. Men's Sixes National Team; the 2025 U.S. Sixes player pool included Pat Kavanagh, Brennan O'Neill, Connor Shellenberger and Michael Sowers.
At the October 2026 Atlas Cup, the U.S. men beat Ireland 35-14 and Canada beat Haudenosaunee 25-14 behind game MVP Zach Currier.
The Haudenosaunee men are ranked fifth in men's sixes; as of November 2026 the IOC had not given a timetable for a decision on their eligibility for the 2028 Games.

facts: The women's individual semifinal at the 2028 Games is scheduled for Saturday, July 15, 2028, 9:00-13:30 Pacific Time at Valley Complex 2 in the Valley Zone, formerly the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, in the San Fernando Valley.
Modern pentathlon opens the 2028 Games program over the first four days (July 15-18) for the first time since 1992, with the women's and men's semifinals on the first two days.

Each semifinal has 18 athletes and runs in this order: direct-elimination fencing, obstacle, swimming, then the laser run; the 70m, eight-obstacle head-to-head obstacle race replaces the riding last used at Paris 2024.
Michelle Gulyas (HUN) won gold at Paris 2024, ahead of Elodie Clouvel (FRA) with silver and Seong Seung-Min (KOR) with bronze.
Gulyas missed the 2026 World Championships in Guiyang, China, with injury, after also missing the 2025 World Championships through injury.
Hungary's Blanka Guzi, ranked world No.1, won the 2026 women's world title in Guiyang on August 30, 2026 with 1,485 points, after two straight world silver medals in 2024 and 2025.
Guzi won 2026 World Cups in Cairo and Budapest, took silver in Pazardzhik and bronze at the 2026 European Championships in Istanbul.
Egypt's Farida Khalil, the 2025 world champion, took silver at the 2026 World Championships aged 15 with 1,474 points.
Great Britain's Kerenza Bryson took bronze at the 2026 World Championships with 1,464 points after reaching the final with the last qualifying spot from her semifinal.
Egypt's Jana Attia set a new obstacle racing mark of 25.17 seconds in the 2026 women's world final.
Switzerland's Anna Jurt won the 2026 World Cup Final in Budapest, the first Swiss athlete to win that title since 1990.
China's Yuang Ma placed fifth and Mingyu Zhang eighth at the 2026 World Championships, a sign of rising Chinese depth.

facts: The men's cross-country final is a single mass-start race with no heats, scheduled for July 17, 2028 at the Industry Hills MTB Course in the City of Industry, Los Angeles County, which replaced Bonelli Park in San Dimas as the planned venue.

Organizers describe the Industry Hills course as hillside terrain with technical sections including drops and jumps; detailed route length and elevation profile had not been published as of the 2025 venue announcement.
Tom Pidcock (GBR), gold medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, won the 2026 elite men's XCO world title in Val di Sole, Italy on August 30, 2026 in 1:25:26, his second XCO world title.

At the 2026 world championships Pidcock started from the fifth row of the grid and needed four of eight laps to join the lead group before finishing 17 seconds ahead of Charlie Aldridge (GBR), with Cole Punchard (CAN) third at 31 seconds.

After the 2026 world championships, Pidcock announced he would step away from mountain biking in 2027 to focus on road racing; he has previously stated hopes to race XCO at the 2028 Games and target a third consecutive gold.

Mathieu van der Poel (NED) finished 30th at the 2026 XCO world championships, and two-time defending world champion Alan Hatherly (RSA), the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, finished 27th after puncturing.
Hatherly won back-to-back XCO world titles in 2024 and 2025; in 2025 at Crans-Montana he finished ahead of Simone Avondetto (ITA) and Paris 2024 silver medalist Victor Koretzky (FRA).
Luca Martin (FRA) won the 2026 XCO World Cup overall title, finishing 380 points ahead of Adrien Boichis (FRA), and also won the 2026 XCC World Cup overall title.
Martin's Cannondale Factory Racing team folded at the end of 2026, and he will ride for Decathlon Ford Racing Team in 2027.
Charlie Aldridge (GBR) won the 2026 World Cup finale at Lake Placid in a sprint over Filippo Colombo (SUI), his first World Cup win since the 2025 finale at Mont-Sainte-Anne.

Christopher Blevins (USA), the 2025 XCO and XCC World Cup overall champion, missed the opening 2026 World Cup round in South Korea with a broken collarbone; Victor Koretzky also missed that round through injury.
American Bjorn Riley took third at the 2026 Lenzerheide XCO World Cup, a potential U.S. contender for a home-soil race at the 2028 Games.
Ten-time world champion Nino Schurter (SUI) rode his final world championships in 2025.

facts: The women's 10km at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 17 at Belmont Shore in Long Beach, California, inside the Long Beach Breakwater near the Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier, with the men's race the following day.

The top three finishers in the women's 10km at the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest earn places at the 2028 Games, and remaining spots in the 22-swimmer field are decided mainly at a qualification event planned for spring 2028.
Paris 2024 champion Sharon van Rouwendaal of the Netherlands announced her retirement on September 5, 2025, so the 2028 race will have a new champion.
Paris 2024 silver medalist Moesha Johnson of Australia won the 2025 world 10km title in Singapore, the first world 10km title won by an Australian.

Johnson went unbeaten across the 10km and 3km knockout sprint events on the 2026 World Cup circuit and became the first athlete in World Aquatics history to win every 10km race in a single World Cup season.

Johnson won the 10km at the 2026 Pan Pacific Championships off Long Beach, California, on August 10, 2026, in 1:55:33, ahead of Japan's Airi Ebina and Ichika Kajimoto, giving her a race win in the same host city as the 2028 event.
Johnson opened the 2026/27 World Cup season by winning the Cancun 10km on November 6, 2026, in 2:03:31.20, more than 13 seconds ahead of Airi Ebina, with Ginevra Taddeucci third.
Johnson also won the 3km knockout sprint in Cancun, and the next World Cup stop is in Soma Bay, Egypt, on March 19-20, 2027.

Paris 2024 bronze medalist Ginevra Taddeucci of Italy won her first European 10km title on August 4, 2026, in the River Seine in 2:07:49.90, ahead of Hungary's Viktoria Mihalyvari-Farkas and Italy's Linda Caponi.
Taddeucci took silver behind Johnson in both the 10km and 5km at the 2025 World Championships and won the 2025 World Cup overall women's title.
Japan's Ichika Kajimoto was ranked No. 2 in the world entering the 2026 Pan Pacific Championships, according to SwimSwam.
Monaco's Lisa Pou, the 2025 world 10km bronze medalist, tied for sixth at the 2026 European Championships 10km.
Johnson and Taddeucci are projected to contend in 2028 based on 2025-2026 form, but neither has qualified yet.

facts: The men's 10km at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 18 at Belmont Shore in Long Beach, California, inside the Long Beach Breakwater, one day after the women's race.

The top three in the men's 10km at the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest earn places at the 2028 Games, and remaining spots in the 22-swimmer field are decided mainly at a qualification event planned for spring 2028.

Germany's Florian Wellbrock, the Tokyo 2020 10km champion, won the 2025 world 10km title in Singapore ahead of Italy's Gregorio Paltrinieri and Australia's Kyle Lee, and won four golds at those championships.

Wellbrock won his first European 10km title in the River Seine on August 4, 2026, with a late sprint, ahead of Paris 2024 bronze medalist David Betlehem of Hungary and Paris 2024 silver medalist Oliver Klemet of Germany.
Paltrinieri finished fourth in the 2026 European 10km after a late comeback, and he prioritized open water over the pool in 2026.
Paris 2024 champion Kristof Rasovszky of Hungary ran near the front for much of the 2026 European 10km in the Seine but finished 23rd.

Wellbrock won the men's 10km at the 2026 Pan Pacific Championships off Long Beach, California, on August 10, 2026, in 1:49:51, ahead of Mexico's Paulo Strehlke and Italy's Dario Verani, in a race opened to European entrants.
Americans Joshua Brown, Ivan Puskovitch and Joey Tepper placed fourth through sixth at the 2026 Pan Pacs 10km in Long Beach, all within about 16 seconds of the winner.
David Betlehem won the 10km at the 2026 World Cup stops in Ibiza and Setubal and secured the 2026 World Cup Overall Leader title with the Setubal win.
Wellbrock won the 2026/27 World Cup opener 10km in Cancun in November 2026 in 1:53:55.80, 2.70 seconds ahead of Italy's Domenico Acerenza and 2.90 seconds ahead of Betlehem.
SwimSwam reported in August 2026 that Wellbrock ranked No. 1 in the open water world rankings.
Wellbrock, Betlehem and Paltrinieri are projected to contend in 2028 based on 2025-2026 form, but none has qualified or publicly confirmed a 2028 entry.

facts: Beach sprint coastal rowing at the 2028 Games is held along Belmont Shore in Long Beach on July 24-25, 2028.
The 2028 Games will be the first time a rowing event at the Games is raced on the ocean.
The 2028 Games allocate 64 of rowing's 502 quota places to beach sprints, and each nation can qualify at most one male and one female athlete.
The main qualification event is the 2027 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Oeiras, Portugal, scheduled for 6-9 October 2027, along with continental qualification events.
A beach sprint race includes a run up the sand, a 250m slalom row with two buoys, a 180-degree turn around a final buoy and a row back to shore before a run to the finish.
At the 2026 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Qingdao, Moritz Wolff (GER) set the fastest men's solo time trial, 3.3 seconds ahead of defending champion Chris Bak (USA).
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, Isabella Scammell (AUS) won the women's solo time trial 1 by seven seconds over Raminta Morkunaite (LTU) and Zhu Wenjie (CHN), with Magdalena Lobnig (AUT) fourth.

At the 2025 world finals in Antalya, Wolff was fastest in the men's solo time trials and Emma Twigg (New Zealand) posted the fastest women's time, while defending champions Bak and Lobnig also advanced to the knockouts.
The 2026 time trials in Qingdao were run in difficult surf, with many capsizes, after storms cancelled training and competition over the opening weekend.
The men's solo at the 2026 world finals drew 48 entries, the largest men's solo field in World Rowing beach sprint history.
Samuel Forbes (AUS) was seventh in the 2026 time trials and went on to win men's solo silver, which shows that a seeding position from the time trials does not decide the knockouts.

facts: Chris Bak (USA) won the men's solo at the World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in 2024 and 2025 and is a four-time beach sprint world champion.
After the 2025 world finals, Bak had six World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals medals (four gold, one silver, one bronze), and nobody has won more gold medals.
Bak won the first-ever US beach sprint gold in the men's solo in 2022 in Saundersfoot, Wales.
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, 21-year-old Liu Jiayu (CHN) won the men's solo ahead of 20-year-old Samuel Forbes (AUS), and Moritz Wolff (GER) took bronze over Allison Russo (POR).
Liu Jiayu overcame an equipment failure in the 2026 final when his boat's sliding seat came loose, and he won China's first men's solo world title.
On the way to the 2026 final, Forbes knocked out Bak in the quarterfinals, and Liu beat European champion Ander Martin (ESP).
At the 2025 world finals, Bak beat Ander Martin (ESP) in the men's solo final, after Wolff tripped and fell on the beach run in his semifinal against Martin.
Isabella Scammell (AUS) won the 2026 women's solo world title ahead of Zhu Wenjie (CHN), which was Australia's first gold at any Beach Sprint Finals.
Magdalena Lobnig (AUT) won women's solo bronze in 2026, after gold in 2024 and silver in 2025, and has reached the podium three years in a row.
In the 2026 women's solo knockouts, Christine Cavallo (USA) missed the buzzer in her quarterfinal against Scammell, and Lobnig went the wrong way around a slalom buoy in her semifinal.

At the 2026 Youth Games in Dakar in early November 2026, Liu Lili (CHN) won the under-age women's solo and 16-year-old Callum Dreyer (RSA) was a surprise men's solo winner after rivals capsized or veered off line in the knockouts.
Chris Bak served as an athlete role model for beach sprints at the 2026 Youth Games in Dakar.

Podium finishers in the men's solo, women's solo or mixed double at the 2026 world finals who row for a qualified federation earned automatic individual places in the 2027 World Rowing Beach Sprint Series.
None of these athletes has been confirmed for the 2028 Games, because quota places will be decided mainly at the 2027 world finals in Oeiras, Portugal.

facts: The mixed double sculls at the 2028 Games will be the first mixed-gender rowing event ever held at the Games.

The 2025 mixed double sculls field drew 33 entries, including multi-gold medallist Adrian Miramon Quiroga of Spain and Tokyo 2020 champion Federica Cesarini of Italy.

Su and Liu had also won the under-19 mixed double title at the 2026 world finals in Qingdao.
The 2028 qualification system allows a nation to enter a boat with different athletes from those who earned the quota place at the qualification events.

Results from the last 16 of the three 2028 event classes at the 2026 world finals qualified China, Australia, Germany, Lithuania, Portugal, Spain and the USA for the new World Rowing Beach Sprint Series in 2027.

China's Han Jiayu took women's 10m air rifle silver in Doha with 252.2 and China's Wang Zifei won bronze with 231.0.
France's Oceanne Muller finished fourth in the Doha women's 10m air rifle final with 209.5, earning a 2028 Games quota place for France; India's Elavenil Valarivan was sixth.
At the 2025 World Championship in Cairo, Germany's Maximilian Dallinger won the men's 10m air rifle title with 252, ahead of Sweden's Victor Lindgren.
The 2028 Games session at Long Beach Target Shooting Hall runs qualification and finals for both the women's and men's 10m air rifle on the same day.

facts: The 2028 Games shotgun events will be held at Whittier Narrows Clay Shooting Center in South El Monte, within the Whittier Narrows Recreation Area, while rifle and pistol events go to the Long Beach Target Shooting Hall.
Under the ISSF 2026 Rulebook, skeet finals take eight athletes instead of six, so the top eight from qualification advance to the final.

The first six skeet quota places for the 2028 Games were awarded at the 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha on November 6, 2026: men's places went to Denmark, Egypt and Kuwait, and women's places to China, Slovakia and Kazakhstan.

After the first day of men's skeet qualification in Doha, Denmark's Jesper Hansen, Finland's Eetu Kallioinen, neutral athlete Kirill Makarov and Egypt's Azmy Mehelba were tied for the lead with a perfect 50.
In women's skeet in Doha, Slovakia's Monika Stibrava (fourth) and Kazakhstan's Assem Orynbay (fifth) earned quota places for their countries behind a Chinese podium sweep led by Jiang Yiting.
Vincent Hancock (USA), the Paris 2024 men's skeet champion and reigning world champion, did not compete in men's skeet at the 2026 Doha World Championship.
Hancock has said he intends to go for a fifth men's skeet gold at the 2028 Games, and he set a men's skeet world record of 36 in the final at the 2026 ISSF World Cup in Lonato on July 7, 2026.
As of late 2026, Hancock's ISSF profile listed him at 16th in the men's skeet world rankings.
Christian Elliott (USA) won the 2026 USA Shooting Fall Skeet Selection Match, beating Hancock in the final, but Hancock topped the combined men's skeet national team ranking with 495.
Samantha Simonton (USA) won the 2025 women's skeet world title in Athens and also won the 2026 USA Shooting Fall Skeet Selection Match.

Francisca Crovetto (CHI) is the reigning Paris 2024 women's skeet champion, with Amber Rutter (GBR) silver and Austen Smith (USA) bronze, and Crovetto was entered in the 2026 Doha World Championship field.
Great Britain (Amber Rutter, Bethany Norton, Madeleine Russell) took women's skeet team silver in Doha behind China, with Italy third.

facts: Mixed team trap replaces the Paris 2024 mixed team skeet event on the 2028 Games program; Italy (Diana Bacosi and Gabriele Rossetti) won the one-time mixed skeet title in Paris, ahead of the USA and China.
At the 2028 Games, the top four mixed trap teams from qualification advance directly to one medal final and all shoot at the same time, instead of separate gold and bronze medal matches.
ISSF says the four-team final is meant to keep every medal contender in the contest throughout and to give spectators a clearer storyline.
Italy's Massimo Fabbrizi and Alessia Iezzi won mixed team trap at the 2025 ISSF World Championship in Athens, topping qualification with a combined 145.
San Marino's Gian Marco Berti and Alessandra Perilli took 2025 world silver in mixed team trap after reaching the top two through a four-way shoot-off.
Walton (Glenn) Eller and Ava Downs (USA) won mixed trap bronze at the 2025 World Championship by beating Egypt's Ahmed Zahar and Maggy Ashmawy, and it was Downs's first world medal, at age 20.
Eller's 2025 mixed team bronze was his first world medal in trap, as distinct from double trap.
India's skeet medalist Maheshwari Chauhan said the switch from mixed skeet to mixed trap was disappointing for skeet shooters but that athletes would adapt.
The 2026 Doha World Championship quota places cover the 12 individual events; the mixed team event awards no quota places there.

facts: Women's street at the 2028 Games will field 22 skaters, with preliminary rounds deciding who advances to the final, and is scheduled at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area.

Qualification Phase 1 runs from 11 June 2026 to 31 March 2028 and uses the World Skateboarding Ranking, which counts best World Skateboarding Tour results from the previous 18 months; the WST World Cup Rome in June 2026 was the first points-awarding event.
Japan's Yumeka Oda won the women's street world title at the World Skate Games in Asuncion, Paraguay, on 18 October 2026, her second world title in three years after winning in Tokyo in 2023.
The Asuncion 2026 women's street contest drew 83 entrants and carried 4000 world ranking points for the winner.

Rayssa Leal (BRA), the Paris 2024 bronze medalist and defending World Skate Games champion from 2024, finished seventh in the Asuncion 2026 final with 77.11 after missing all three best-trick attempts.
Brazilian media reported Leal described the Asuncion world championship as a testing ground aimed at the 2028 Games.
Leal won the 2026 SLS season opener in Sydney and the SLS Rio de Janeiro stop in 2026, edging Japan's Momiji Nishiya by 0.02 in Rio; she is a four-time SLS Super Crown champion (2022-2025).
Paris 2024 champion Coco Yoshizawa (JPN) posted a 75-point second run to stay in contention in the Asuncion 2026 final.
Japan's Ibuki Matsumoto won the earlier 2026 world title in Sao Paulo (March 2026) and her first WST title at Kitakyushu in November 2025 at age 13.
Chloe Covell (AUS) won the WST Rome street World Cup in both 2025 and 2026, scoring 177.01 in the 2026 final, and also contested the Asuncion 2026 final.
Oda finished second at both Kitakyushu 2025 and Rome 2026 before her Asuncion win.
Paige Heyn was the top American at Rome 2026 in fourth, and China's Chenxi Cui took her first WST podium there in third.

facts: Yuto Horigome of Japan won men's Street gold at Paris 2024, defending his Tokyo 2020 title, with Jagger Eaton (USA) taking silver and Nyjah Huston (USA) bronze.

Brazil's Giovanni Vianna put down strong runs in the Asuncion 2026 final, including a third run of 85 points, but did not land enough in the best trick section.
The WST Street World Cup in Rome in June 2026 was the first qualifying event for the 2028 Games and marked the official start of the skateboarding qualification period.

facts: Surfing at the 2028 Games will be held at Lower Trestles, a high-performance cobblestone break in San Clemente, California.
Organizers chose Lower Trestles over Huntington Beach to host surfing's third appearance at the Games.
The 2028 surfing field is 48 athletes, 24 men and 24 women, and each nation can qualify up to three surfers per gender, up from two at Paris 2024.
The 2026 ISA World Surfing Games, held November 6-15, 2026 at Punta Rocas, Peru, is the first ISA event to award places for the 2028 Games.
At the 2026 ISA World Surfing Games, the highest-ranked men's team and highest-ranked women's team each earn one 2028 place for their nation, with athletes then selected by the national committee.
The ISA reported 230 surfers from 52 nations at the 2026 World Surfing Games, including 30 previous Games competitors and five past medalists.
Because most places are allocated through later pathways, including the 2028 ISA World Surfing Games, the full Round 1 field is not expected to be known until shortly before the Games.
The host nation is guaranteed one place per gender unless it already fills that place through another pathway.
Universality places require the nominated athlete to finish in the top 40 at the 2027 or 2028 ISA World Surfing Games, so smaller surfing nations may appear in the opening round.
Team USA's six-surfer squad at the 2026 World Surfing Games is Gabriela Bryan, Carissa Moore, Sawyer Lindblad, Griffin Colapinto, Cole Houshmand and Crosby Colapinto.
USA Surfing states there is no discretionary selection for the 2028 team; places are filled by published selection procedures.
USA Surfing head coach Ryan Simmons has said the team is targeting additional qualifying spots and that many American surfers regularly train at Trestles.
Host-team Peru's Lucca Mesinas and Catalina Zariquiey posted event-high scores on Day 3 of the 2026 World Surfing Games.

At Paris 2024, held at Teahupo'o, Kauli Vaast (FRA) won men's gold ahead of Jack Robinson (AUS) and Gabriel Medina (BRA), and Caroline Marks (USA) won women's gold ahead of Tatiana Weston-Webb (BRA) and Johanne Defay (FRA).

facts: Swimming at the 2028 Games is held in a temporary pool inside SoFi Stadium, called 2028 Stadium during the Games, and the pool program runs July 22-30, 2028.
Swimming moves to the second week of the 2028 Games, swapping places with athletics.

This opening morning session includes heats of the new men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke, two of six 50m stroke events approved in April 2025 that use a heats, semifinals and final format.
Relays and the 800m/1500m freestyle go straight from heats to finals, so the men's and women's 4x100m freestyle relay heats this morning set the lanes for that evening's finals.

Gretchen Walsh, the 100m butterfly world record holder and Paris 2024 silver medalist, won the 100m butterfly at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore in a championship-record 54.73, the second-fastest time in history.
Summer McIntosh beat Katie Ledecky to win the women's 400m freestyle at the 2025 World Championships in Singapore.
Paris 2024 women's 400m freestyle champion Ariarne Titmus of Australia retired from swimming on October 16, 2025, aged 25, so the 2028 event will have a new champion.
Paris 2024 men's 400m freestyle champion Lukas Märtens of Germany took bronze in the 800m freestyle at the 2025 World Championships, behind Tunisia's Ahmed Jaouadi and Germany's Sven Schwarz.
Nicolò Martinenghi won the men's 100m breaststroke at Paris 2024, while Adam Peaty tied for silver, so no bronze was awarded.
The United States won a meet-leading nine swimming golds at the 2025 World Championships.

facts: This day-two morning session at 2028 Stadium (SoFi Stadium) has heats of the women's 100m breaststroke, men's 100m backstroke, women's 100m freestyle and men's 400m IM.

Tatjana Smith (formerly Schoenmaker), 29, retired after Paris 2024, announced a comeback around September 2026 aimed at the 2028 Games, and on November 10, 2026 said she will switch her international allegiance from South Africa to the Netherlands.
Smith holds dual South African and Dutch citizenship and cited financial challenges and better high-performance support as reasons for the switch.
Leon Marchand won the men's 400m IM at Paris 2024 and won it again at the 2025 World Championships in Singapore in 4:04.73, well ahead of Tomoyuki Matsushita.
Tomoyuki Matsushita of Japan was runner-up to Marchand in the 400m IM at both Paris 2024 and the 2025 World Championships.

Marchand suffered an adductor injury at the French Championships in June 2026 but went on to win gold at the 2026 European Championships in Paris, and he leads France's team for the December 2026 World Short Course Championships in Beijing.
Sarah Sjöström won the women's 100m freestyle at Paris 2024 ahead of Torri Huske and Siobhán Haughey.
Kate Douglass became the first woman under 50 seconds in the short-course 100m freestyle on the 2025 World Cup circuit, and Gretchen Walsh ranks third all-time with 50.31, per Swimming World.
Torri Huske swam on the US women's 4x100m medley relay that set a 3:49.34 world record at the 2025 World Championships.

facts: Friday, July 21 at Court 1 combines singles first-round matches with the opening day of men's and women's doubles.
Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19 to 28 on outdoor hard courts at Carson Courts, inside the Dignity Health Sports Park complex in Carson, California.
Men's singles runs July 20-28, women's singles July 20-27, men's doubles July 21-27 and women's doubles July 21-28.
For doubles entry, players in the doubles top 10 get priority, and the remaining places go by combined ranking, the sum of each partner's best singles or doubles ranking.
Paris 2024 women's doubles champions Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini of Italy won the 2025 Roland Garros women's doubles title, their first major title as a team.
Paolini pulled out of the 2026 Rome doubles with a foot problem, so the pair could not defend that title.
Errani retired from singles in May 2025 and took up professional padel, but has kept playing Grand Slam mixed doubles and has coached Paolini since December 2025.
Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider took Paris 2024 women's doubles silver as neutral athletes, and Spain won bronze.

Matthew Ebden and John Peers won Paris 2024 men's doubles gold for Australia, beating Americans Rajeev Ram and Austin Krajicek 10-8 in the match tiebreak, and Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul took bronze for the United States.
Alexander Zverev, who won Roland Garros and the US Open in 2026, became ATP world No. 1 in early November 2026.
Jannik Sinner was ranked No. 2 as of November 2, 2026, after retaking No. 1 from Alcaraz in April 2026 and later ending his season early with a knee injury.
Elena Rybakina reached WTA world No. 1 in 2026 after winning the Australian Open and US Open, along with a Stuttgart title, and had a 54-14 record.

facts: The women's individual triathlon on Saturday, July 15, 2028 at 7:30am is scheduled to award the first medals of the 2028 Games, the first time triathlon has opened the medal schedule since Sydney 2000.
The transition area and finish line at Venice Beach will be staged where Venice Boulevard meets the sand.
The individual swim starts from the beach rather than a pontoon, with a 1,000m lap, a 25m beach run and a 500m second lap.
The 40km bike leg is eight 5km laps with two technical turnaround points, followed by a four-lap 10km run through the Venice canals area.
A World Triathlon test event on the 2028 course in Venice Beach is planned for July 2027.

Individual quota places will be allocated mainly from the Individual Qualification Ranking of May 18, 2028, with the top 21 ranked athletes per gender earning places for their nations, and the United States as host guaranteed two places per gender.
A nation may enter a maximum of three athletes per gender only if at least three of its athletes are inside the top 30 of the qualification ranking on May 18, 2028.
Cassandre Beaugrand (FRA), the Paris 2024 champion, went unbeaten in the 2026 WTCS season and won the Pontevedra Grand Final on Sept 26, 2026 to claim her second world title after her first in 2024.
In the 2026 WTCS London race, Beaugrand won in 56:06, five seconds ahead of Lisa Tertsch (GER) and 15 seconds ahead of Tilda Månsson (SWE).
Beaugrand did not finish the 2025 Wollongong Grand Final, where Lisa Tertsch (GER) won the race and the 2025 world title.
In the final 2025 WTCS standings, Léonie Périault (FRA) was second and Paris 2024 bronze medalist Beth Potter (GBR) was third.

Taylor Knibb (USA) returned to standard-distance racing in 2026, placing 11th at a WTCS race in Italy in May and collecting qualification points toward the 2028 Games, and also won a US national time trial title on the bike.
Knibb won the 2026 Ironman World Championship in Kona and was then second to Velasquez at the Iquique World Cup on Nov 8, 2026.
Rio 2016 champion Gwen Jorgensen (USA) trained at Venice Beach in 2026 while preparing for a possible appearance at a home Games.

facts: The mixed team event makes its debut at the 2028 Games and replaces the separate men's and women's team events used from Beijing 2008 through Paris 2024.
The IOC Executive Board approved the mixed team event in April 2025, which brought table tennis to six medal events, more than any other racket sport at the 2028 Games.
The mixed team format was first used at the ITTF Mixed Team World Cup in Chengdu in December 2023.
At the 2028 Games the mixed team event starts with a group stage of four groups, followed by quarterfinals, semifinals and the bronze and gold medal matches.

At the Mixed Team World Cup, ties are played as a series of doubles and singles matches with games counted cumulatively, and the lower-ranked team's captain chooses whether men's or women's doubles is played first in the closing doubles matches.

facts: The men's 110kg final is a single-session medal event at the Peacock Theater on Friday, July 28, from 8:50 PM to 11:00 PM.
Men's 110kg is a new bodyweight category for the 2028 Games and did not exist at Paris 2024.
Uzbekistan's Akbar Djuraev won the 2026 world 110kg title in Ningbo with world records of 198kg in the snatch and 432kg in the total, his fourth world title.
Djuraev missed only his final clean and jerk attempt, 238kg, which would also have been a world record.
Iran's Alireza Nassiri took 2026 world silver at 110kg with 418kg, and Turkmenistan's Sahzadbek Matyakubow took bronze with 417kg.
China's Liu Huanhua, the Paris 2024 men's heavyweight champion, finished sixth at 110kg in Ningbo with 180-225-405, 27kg behind Djuraev.
Liu competed in the B Group in Ningbo after fitness problems, according to the IWF.
The 2026 World Championships were the first of 10 qualifying events for the 2028 Games; the qualification window runs from July 27, 2026 to May 7, 2028.
Weightlifting at the 2028 Games is capped at 60 men across six men's categories, and 96 of 120 total spots are awarded through the qualification ranking.

facts: The men's +110kg final is a single-session medal event at the Peacock Theater on Saturday, July 29, from 4:50 PM to 7:00 PM.
Men's +110kg replaces the Paris 2024 super-heavyweight division as the top men's category.
Georgia's Lasha Talakhadze won his third straight super-heavyweight title at Paris 2024 with a 470kg total; Armenia's Varazdat Lalayan took silver and Bahrain's Gor Minasyan took bronze.
Talakhadze came out of retirement aiming for a fourth straight Games title and was entered at the 2026 World Championships in Ningbo, his first international meet since Paris.
Iraq's Ali Ammar won the 2026 world +110kg title with a 466kg total, becoming Iraq's first world champion in any sport on the Games program, according to the IWF.
Iran's Alireza Yousefi took 2026 world silver at +110kg with 458kg and set a 263kg clean and jerk world record; Lalayan took bronze with 457kg.
Talakhadze did not finish on the 2026 world +110kg podium.
After the IWF's bodyweight category changes, Talakhadze's 225kg snatch world record was annulled, and Ali Ammar's 219kg snatch became the recognized world record.

facts: This session is among the opening men's preliminary matches of the 2028 tournament, with two group-stage games on July 12.
Water polo at the 2028 Games will be held at the Long Beach Aquatics Center, a temporary open-air facility built for the Games that will also host artistic swimming.

The 2028 men's tournament has 12 teams in three groups of four, with the top two in each group plus the two best third-placed teams reaching the quarterfinals, and the United States qualifies automatically as host.
Serbia won the Paris 2024 gold, beating Croatia 13-11 in the final, while the United States took bronze by beating Hungary.
Water polo at the 2028 Games runs from July 12, with the men's final on July 22 and the women's gold medal match closing the tournament on July 23.

Greece beat Hungary 15-14 in the 2026 World Cup final in Sydney on July 26, 2026, its first major men's international title, with captain Stylianos Argyropoulos scoring the winner with 12.7 seconds left.

facts: This session holds the round of 16 and quarterfinals in men's freestyle 57kg and 86kg and women's freestyle 62kg, plus repechage bouts for the day-three classes (GR 67kg, GR 87kg, W FS 57kg).
Japan's Rei Higuchi won men's freestyle 57kg gold at Paris 2024, beating Spencer Lee of the USA in the final.
Spencer Lee's silver medal at Paris 2024 makes him a returning medalist for the host nation at 57kg if he qualifies.
Bulgaria's Magomed Ramazanov won men's freestyle 86kg gold at Paris 2024.
USA's Kyle Dake won the 2026 world title at men's freestyle 86kg, beating Azerbaijan's Arsenii Dzhioev in the final; Georgia's Vladimeri Gamkrelidze and Kyrgyzstan's Malik Shavaev took bronze.
Japan's Sakura Motoki won women's freestyle 62kg gold at Paris 2024.
Japan won eight golds across all three styles at Paris 2024, including four in women's freestyle.
Each nation may enter only one wrestler per weight class, with places earned through United World Wrestling qualifying events.

facts: This evening session holds the semifinals in men's freestyle 57kg and 86kg and women's freestyle 62kg, plus the medal matches in Greco-Roman 67kg, Greco-Roman 87kg and women's freestyle 57kg.
Greco-Roman 67kg: Iran's Saeid Esmaeili won Paris 2024 gold and the 2025 and 2026 world titles, beating Uzbekistan's Aytjan Khalmakhanov in the 2026 final.
Greco-Roman 67kg: Azerbaijan's Hasrat Jafarov took 2025 world silver and won the 2026 European title.
Greco-Roman 87kg: Bulgaria's Semen Novikov is the Paris 2024 champion and won the 2026 world title.
Greco-Roman 87kg: Serbia's Aleksandr Komarov won the 2025 world title, with Iran's Alireza Mohmadi second.
Women's freestyle 57kg: Japan's Tsugumi Sakurai is the Paris 2024 champion.
Women's freestyle 57kg: USA's Helen Maroulis, the 2025 world champion at 57kg, took bronze at 57kg at the 2026 World Championships after losing a 4-2 quarterfinal to Japan's Sena Nagamoto.
Men's freestyle 57kg semifinals: Japan's Rei Higuchi beat USA's Spencer Lee in the Paris 2024 final.
Men's freestyle 86kg semifinals: Bulgaria's Magomed Ramazanov is the Paris 2024 champion, and USA's Kyle Dake won the 2026 world title at 86kg.
Greco-Roman wraps up around July 27, while men's and women's freestyle continue through July 30.

facts: This session covers the round of 16 and quarterfinals in men's freestyle 65kg and 97kg and women's freestyle 76kg, plus repechage bouts for the classes that have medal matches later the same day.
Japan's Kotaro Kiyooka won the men's freestyle 65kg gold at Paris 2024.
Iran's Rahman Amouzad won the 2025 world 65kg title in Zagreb, beating Kotaro Kiyooka in the final; Real Woods of the USA took bronze.
USA's Bo Bassett won the 2026 world title at men's freestyle 65kg in Astana.
Bahrain's Akhmed Tazhudinov won the men's freestyle 97kg gold at Paris 2024 and was the 2023 world champion at 97kg.
Kyle Snyder of the USA won the 2025 world title at 97kg, beating Iran's Amir Ali Azarpira 4-2 in the final; Azarpira had beaten Snyder 4-1 in the Paris 2024 bronze-medal match.
Kyle Snyder was the U.S. entrant at 97kg at the 2026 World Championships.

Reports on the 2026 world 97kg final conflict: one results list shows Bahrain's Akhmed Tazhudinov beating Georgia's Givi Matcharashvili 2-0 for gold and Iran's Amir Ali Azarpira beating Kyle Snyder for bronze, while a FloWrestling team standings page lists Snyder as gold.
Abdulrashid Sadulaev won the 2026 European title at 97kg, with Slovakia's Batyrbek Tsakulov second.
Japan's Yuka Kagami won the women's freestyle 76kg gold at Paris 2024, beating Kennedy Blades of the USA in the final.
Kennedy Blades was entered at 68kg, not 76kg, in the 2026 U.S. Final X series, and Kylie Welker was the U.S. entrant in the 76kg Final X matchup.

facts: This evening session has the semifinals in men's freestyle 65kg and 97kg and women's freestyle 76kg, followed by the bronze-medal matches and gold-medal finals in men's freestyle 74kg and 125kg and women's freestyle 68kg.
Uzbekistan's Razambek Zhamalov won the men's freestyle 74kg gold at Paris 2024.
Japan's Kota Takahashi won the 2025 world 74kg title, with Albania's Chermen Valiev second and Zaurbek Sidakov among the bronze medalists.
Georgia's Geno Petriashvili won the men's freestyle 125kg gold at Paris 2024.
Iran's Amir Hossein Zare, the Paris 2024 silver medalist at 125kg, won world titles in 2025 and 2026; in the 2026 final in Astana he beat Abdulla Kurbanov.
Azerbaijan's Giorgi Meshvildishvili and USA's Wyatt Hendrickson took 2026 world bronze at 125kg.
Gable Steveson of the USA, who won 125kg gold at Tokyo 2020, has said he would like to win gold at the 2028 Games, but in 2026 he said his UFC career is now his priority.
Amit Elor of the USA won the women's freestyle 68kg gold at Paris 2024 at age 20, becoming the youngest U.S. wrestling gold medalist at the Games.

Elor moved up to 72kg, a weight not contested at the Games, in 2025, announced in September 2025 that she was pregnant, and won the 72kg U.S. World Team Trials Challenge tournament in May 2026 three months after giving birth.
Kennedy Blades, the Paris 2024 silver medalist at 76kg, was entered at 68kg in the 2026 U.S. Final X series against Isabella Mir.
Men's freestyle 65kg semifinals: USA's Bo Bassett won the 2026 world title at 65kg.

facts: This session has the repechage bouts, both bronze-medal matches and the gold-medal finals in men's freestyle 65kg and 97kg and women's freestyle 76kg.
Each weight class awards two bronze medals, decided through a repechage for wrestlers who lost to the two finalists.
Japan's Kotaro Kiyooka won 65kg gold at Paris 2024, then took 2025 world silver after losing the final to Iran's Rahman Amouzad.
USA's Bo Bassett won the 2026 world title at 65kg, a year after USA's Real Woods took 2025 world bronze at the weight.
Bahrain's Akhmed Tazhudinov won 97kg gold at Paris 2024 and took bronze at the 2025 World Championships.
Kyle Snyder of the USA, the 2016 gold medalist at 97kg, won his fourth world title in 2025 by beating Iran's Amir Ali Azarpira 4-2, after losing 4-1 to Azarpira in the Paris 2024 bronze-medal match.

Reports on the 2026 world 97kg final conflict: one results list shows Bahrain's Akhmed Tazhudinov beating Georgia's Givi Matcharashvili 2-0 for gold and Iran's Amir Ali Azarpira beating Kyle Snyder for bronze, while a FloWrestling team standings page lists Snyder as gold.
Abdulrashid Sadulaev, the 2016 and 2020 gold medalist at 97kg, won the 2026 European title at 97kg.
U.S. men's freestyle wrestlers at the 2026 World Championships included Trent Hidlay, who took silver at 92kg, and Wyatt Hendrickson, who took bronze at 125kg.
Japan's Yuka Kagami won women's freestyle 76kg gold at Paris 2024, beating Kennedy Blades of the USA in the final.
Blades competed at 68kg rather than 76kg in the 2026 U.S. Final X series, where Kylie Welker was the U.S. 76kg entrant.
